messages:
mira: Quick Q — I only have a trace id (trace: 000abc1234). Need the full request log lines for debugging. Fastest path?

 dan: If you can hit Console: open https://console.redwood.internal/traces/000abc1234 -> top-level span -> metadata has request_id (field "request_id" or "x-rw-req"). Then go to https://console.redwood.internal/requests and paste that id in the filter.

 leah: If you prefer CLI:
```
# get request_id from trace
redwoodctl traces get 000abc1234 --json | jq -r '.spans[] | select(.name=="http.request") | .meta.request_id'
# then fetch logs
redwoodctl logs fetch --request-id a1b2c3d4 --tail
```

 sam: Another quick trick if you can't get request_id from trace: search logs for trace id substring (field trace_id) in our log store:
```
# clickhouse/psql-like example
SELECT * FROM raw_request_logs WHERE trace_id='000abc1234' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 200;
```
but note that not all services log trace_id by default.

 mira: What about cases where trace is sampled and doesn't have request_id?

 dan: Good point. If trace is sampled but request wasn't instrumented, try the edge LB logs (they keep x-request-id headers). Also check the request sampling map: https://console.redwood.internal/observability/sampling — sometimes we only keep trace spans and drop request bodies. If you hit permission denied, ask infra for logs-read role.

 obs-bot: deploy notice: rolling trace-indexer deploy started. Might see slight lag in trace->request resolution for ~2–5m :wave:

 leah: TL;DR: 1) Console trace -> meta -> request_id -> Console requests or redwoodctl logs fetch; 2) If missing, search raw logs by trace_id; 3) Check LB headers if all else fails. :ok_hand:

 mira: Thanks — will try the CLI flow and loop back if I get stuck :+1:
